findings.claim: The app/reader pools still authenticate as the postgres superuser; only the session GUC role downgrades the effective principal to role_app_backend. RLS is genuinely enforced today because pg sends options=-c role=role_app_backend in the startup packet and node-postgres never issues DISCARD ALL or RESET on release (RESET role would return to role_app_backend anyway, since the startup value is the session default), but session authorization remains superuser, so any future code path that executes SET ROLE postgres or SET SESSION AUTHORIZATION silently restores BYPASSRLS, and no CI step asserts the effective principal.
findings.fix: Add a cheap assertion that pins the sensor: in backend:rls-smoke or in the app e2e bootstrap, query select current_user, (select usesuper from pg_user where usename = session_user) through the app pool and fail unless current_user = role_app_backend. Longer term, provision a dedicated LOGIN role for app/reader in CI instead of a GUC downgrade of postgres.

findings.claim: In local/test profiles detranDataOptions falls back to DATABASE_URL when STYNX_APP_DATABASE_URL is absent, and the distinct-principal guard at line 232 only runs when the profile is non-local. A typo, rename or accidental removal of the three new workflow variables therefore re-creates the exact superuser-bypass sensor failure being corrected here, with the whole suite still reporting green because the cross-tenant fixture would once more be visible only in a test that already expects isolation.
findings.fix: Make the test profile fail closed: when DETRAN_RUNTIME_PROFILE is test (or NODE_ENV=test) require STYNX_APP_DATABASE_URL/STYNX_READER_DATABASE_URL explicitly, or reject an app connection whose effective principal is a superuser, instead of silently reusing DATABASE_URL.

findings.claim: STYNX_READER_DATABASE_URL reuses role_app_backend, which holds SELECT, INSERT, UPDATE and DELETE on auth, tenancy, storage, integration, inf, est, ch and ops (backend/database/ddl/20-rls-policies.sql:29). The reader pool in CI is therefore not least-privilege and a read-path regression that writes through the reader connection would not be caught.
findings.fix: Point the reader pool at a read-only principal (for example options=-c role=role_auditor_min, after granting it the SELECT it needs), so the CI reader pool reproduces the production separation the non-local guard demands.

notes: Mechanism verified end to end: pg-connection-string 2.14.0 keeps the options query parameter (index.js parses searchParams, and the pre-encoding regex is not triggered by %20/%3D, so the decoded value is exactly -c role=role_app_backend), pg 8.23.0 forwards params.options into the startup packet (lib/client.js:567), and @stynx-nyx/data 1.3.1 passes connectionString straight into new pg.Pool (dist/data/src/pools.js createPoolConfig), so no parsing layer drops it.

Enforcement is real, not cosmetic: role_app_backend is created NOSUPERUSER NOBYPASSRLS (backend/database/ddl/01-schemas.sql:15), auth.create_rls_policy applies ENABLE plus FORCE ROW LEVEL SECURITY with USING (tenant_id = auth.current_tenant()) (backend/database/ddl/11-auth-functions.sql:53-58), ops.agency_unit is covered (backend/database/ddl/13-ops-agency.sql:58), and auth.current_tenant() reads app.tenant_id, which is exactly the GUC @stynx-nyx/data sets per request with set_config(..., true). A superuser app pool bypassed all of that, which matches the observed PR #40 failure.

Privileges for the downgraded pool are present rather than accidental: each generated DDL file re-grants schema/table/sequence access to role_app_backend, and 20-rls-policies.sql:28-39 grants audit.write EXECUTE while revoking auth.set_current_tenant, which the runtime does not need because it uses set_config directly. This is consistent with the reported full green rerun.

No test, DDL, policy or gate was weakened: the diff 35034fa..7a62d8f touches only three env lines in .github/workflows/ci.yml plus append-only evidence. backend/app/tests/e2e/ops-modules.e2e.spec.ts is unchanged and its cross-tenant assertion stays unconditional (expects []); its superuser client is used only through DETRAN_TEST_DATABASE_URL to plant the other-tenant fixture with app.role=owner, which is the fixture channel and not the assertion channel.

The first FAIL is not hidden: R-0005.jsonl sequence 4 records result FAIL with classification sensor-error, the failing spec and the superuser-bypass observation, and work/rounds/R-0005/plan.md Triagem repeats it verbatim. Sequences 1-3 are untouched.
